guidance.summary: CoreCivic updated its full-year 2026 guidance. The update reflects four facility sales to ICE, which produce an expected ~$1.8 billion gain in Q3 2026 and ~$1.6 billion in net proceeds, and debt repayments that leave about $739.1 million outstanding. The Prairie Facility activation is expected to pressure H2 2026 margins, have an immaterial effect on 2026 earnings and generate about $75 million in annual revenue once fully activated; planned 2026 capital expenditures are specified by category.

guidance.sentence: We anticipate these facilities will continue to contribute to an increase in operating margins in future quarters as we expect the occupancy at these facilities to continue to increase.

We expect the activation of the 1,600-bed Prairie Correctional Facility (Prairie Facility), as further described hereinafter, to negatively impact margins during the second half of 2026 as we hire staff and incur expenses to prepare to receive detainees.
The gross sales price for these four facility sales totals $2.2 billion, resulting in an aggregate gain on sale of approximately $1.8 billion to be reported in the third quarter of 2026.
After federal and state income taxes of approximately $0.5 billion and transaction costs, we anticipate our net proceeds from the facility sales to be approximately $1.6 billion.
Following these debt repayments, the Company’s total debt outstanding is expected to be approximately $739.1 million.
Taking into account start-up activities and the phased commencement of intake operations, we currently expect an immaterial impact to earnings for the remainder of 2026.

writeup.headline: CoreCivic rates Hold: strong growth and momentum offset by a weak balance sheet and full valuation.
writeup.thesis: CoreCivic scores 54, a Hold, sitting 11 points below Buy and 10 points above Sell. Growth (77) and trend (80) are the strengths, with TTM revenue growth of 24.4%, latest-quarter revenue growth of 27.3% year on year, and shares 40.0 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. Quality is middling at 59: the operating margin is 9.9% but the FCF margin is only 2.4%, helped by a diluted share count down 9.0% year on year. The balance sheet scores just 4, with net debt at 21.17 times free cash flow and cash covering only 0.08 of debt. Valuation scores 30: P/FCF of 51.4 is high in absolute terms, the FCF yield is 3.0 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and the stock is expensive against its own history, more expensive than at 54 of the last 61 month-ends on P/S.
key_risks: Heavy dependence on ICE, which can terminate contracts at facilities CoreCivic has sold to it
Thin free cash flow relative to debt (net debt 21.17 times FCF) leaves little cushion
Valuation is expensive against its own history, and P/FCF of 51.4 is high in absolute terms
Prairie Facility activation is expected to pressure second-half 2026 margins
Shares are already 13.8% below their 52-week high and 6.6% below the 50-day average, so momentum could fade
what_would_change: Up to Buy (11 points needed): a much stronger balance sheet score, for example if the ~$1.6 billion in sale proceeds and debt paydown to about $739.1 million show up in filed results
Up: better free cash flow conversion lifting quality and valuation scores, or positive guidance with Q3 results on 2026-11-04
Down to Sell (10 points away): growth slowing sharply or the trend score breaking down as the share price weakens further
Down: an adverse ICE contract or policy change, such as more consolidation into government-owned sites, turning news risk negative
